envSeams.name: OMO_COMPUTER_BACKEND
envSeams.purpose: selects the backend; `fake` admits the fake-only seams

envSeams.name: OMO_COMPUTER_FAKE_SCENARIO
envSeams.purpose: selects the fake backend's scenario file

envSeams.name: OMO_COMPUTER_RUNTIME_DIR
envSeams.purpose: moves the marker and stop files into a test directory

envSeams.name: OMO_COMPUTER_DISABLE_SKYLIGHT
envSeams.purpose: turns the macOS SkyLight capture route off

envSeams.name: OMO_COMPUTER_UPDATE_SCHEMA
envSeams.purpose: rewrites the generated schema and protocol doc

envSeams.name: OMO_COMPUTER_CONFORMANCE_DIR
envSeams.purpose: points the conformance replay at a fixture directory

envSeams.name: OMO_COMPUTER_BUILD_SHA
envSeams.purpose: the commit the engine was built from

observation.description: Required on the wire: a report without `{untrustedText: true}` does not parse.

ActionReport.description: Everything a report says, before validation.

AppSource.description: Where an `apps.list()` entry came from on this OS.

AuditLine.description: One `audit` line as v1 hosts read it. Text is recorded by length and digest only.

AxSnapshotText.description: The v1 accessibility snapshot: the rendered tree text.

CapabilitiesReply.description: `capabilities`: the v1 record in null mode, the object-mode record otherwise.

CaptureCaps.description: v1 capture caps: the frame is scaled to fit.

crosshair.description: Draws a crosshair at this point in the space `click` consumes (acceptance 90).

CaptureReply.description: `capture` / `zoom`: the v1 frame in null mode, a `Frame` in object mode.

ChainLink.description: One process of the spawn chain with its session context.

ClickParams.description: `click`: a point (v1) or a ref; `consume` asks for a consumption receipt.

ClipboardContent.description: `clipboard.read`: a concealed clipboard answers `{secure:true, text:null, reason:"concealed"}`.

CodeIdentity.description: The code identity consent is bound to (principle 6).

Compositor.description:
The Linux compositor, declared once. `sessionLockProtocol` says the compositor
advertises `ext-session-lock-v1`; the lock datum itself is `session.screenLocked`.

CuaAdapter.description: `cua_adapter`: the tri-state, plus the old boolean read as `on` / `off` for two minor releases.

CursorMode.description: Whose pointer the pixels carry: the OS one, one the engine composited, or none.

Cut.description: A cut container the skeleton did not open; `drill(ref)` opens it.

Delivered.description: How many units of an interrupted send went out.

Delivery.description: The delivery route the model asked for; omitted lets the engine pick.

truncated.description: A display was dropped from the composite.

Disposition.description: Whether input reached the target and whether the same request may be sent again: exactly one of the seven valid (delivery, retry) pairs.

oneOf.description: A receipt for this verb proves the requested effect.
The engine read the target after the send; the read is not proof the input caused it.
Part of the request landed; `delivered` carries the counts.
Nothing proves or reads the effect.
Sent exactly once into a childless hit in a suspect viewport, and nothing changed.
Kept in the union so older shapes still parse; the engine never produces it.

Effect.description: What the engine can say the action did.

ElementInfo.description: One accessibility element as a tree, `find()`, `elementAt()` or a menu shows it.

EpochChanged.description: `epoch.changed`: the frames and refs of an older epoch are stale.

oneOf.description: Windows hook-free barrier: the target dequeued the input.
X11 MPX raw XI2 event: the server consumed and re-emitted the input.
The target's value read back after the send.
The focused element read back after the send.
The menu state read back after the send.
An event from an observer registered on the target window before the send.
Pixels changed in the hit region or the window during the settle window.
A window-wide accessibility change during the settle window.

ExecReply.description: null in a null-mode session; the ActionReport in an object-mode session.

FleetSettings.description: `fleet`: the brain-side fanout budgets. `maxInFlight` is the fanout concurrency.

FocusRestoration.description: Where focus ended after the action. A background action touches no focus: `untouched`.

FrameArtifact.description: Present only when the bytes did not ride inline (size above `limits.maxResponseBytes`).

HandStatus.description: `hand.status`: liveness of the hand the host serves.

generation.description: Incremented on every engine restart; a reply from another generation is quarantined.

machineId.description: sha256-16 of the lock-file identity and the uid: one id per user and machine.

Hit.description: The element read under the point before the send.

LegacyObservation.description: The v1 `observe` reply: a frame plus the accessibility summary.

Limits.description: The size ceilings a host must respect on this connection.

MenuItems.description: `menu.items`: the menu tree, listed without opening, moving or focusing anything.

ObserveAx.description: v1 `observe.ax`: a node budget; the object mode's `ax` flag is the boolean.

ObserveOptions.description: The one observe option set (`observeAfter` and `apps.open{observe}` carry it too).

ObserveReply.description: `observe`: the v1 frame-plus-summary in null mode, an `Observation` in object mode.

ObserveRequest.description: `observe` on `apps.open`: an option set or `true` for the defaults.

Point.description: A point in the coordinate space of the frame the call names (or the latest one).

PointerPosition.description: `pointer`: the pointer position in desktop coordinates.

Rect.description: A rectangle in the coordinate space of the reply that carries it.

ReportMode.description: `reportMode`: `"null"` keeps every v1 reply byte-identical; `"object"` opts into reports.

RequestId.description: A JSON-RPC request id: a number or a string, echoed verbatim.

Route.description: The delivery route the input took.

RunLimits.description:
`run_limits`: the QuickJS cell's ceilings. Every member is overridable per hand; an
omitted member keeps its default.

Runtime.description: `computer.runtime` (amendment A10): which implementation serves the tool until cutover.

SessionOpenParams.description: `session.open`: the v1 session keys plus the `computer.*` settings table.

SessionPauseReason.description: The four reasons a session reports; `screen_locked` and `system_suspended` pause.

authMessage.description: macOS only: absent elsewhere, `null` when no candidate accepted.

SessionProbes.description: The OS symbol or protocol behind each `SessionState` field (`"none"` where there is none).

Settings.description: The one documented `computer.*` table; [`super::SETTINGS_TABLE`] names each key's reader.

StopPathStatus.description: The stop path's state (`stopPath.*` replies and the `stopPath.changed` notification).

SurfaceKind.description: The nineteen system surface kinds; `capabilities().surfaces` lists this OS's subset.

TextRange.description: `selectText`: an index range or the text to select.

Tier.description: The tool tier the `--mcp` shim grants.

Timings.description: Stage timings in microseconds; a stage that did not run is absent.

Trace.description:
`trace`: `false | true | "full"`. `true` writes the JSONL trace only; `"full"` adds the
session manifest and the per-turn artifacts.

UnknownLiteral.description: The literal `"unknown"`: the OS gave no answer, which never refuses and is reported.

UntrustedText.description: The typed prompt-injection signal: screen-derived text in this record is data.

WaitPredicate.description: One `waitFor` predicate; each is bounded by the call's `timeout`.

WaitResult.description: `waitFor`: the outcome and the observation it ended on.

WindowIdentity.description: A window's identity: the OS handle plus the process generation.

z.description: Front-to-back index of the listing order.

WindowInfo.description: One `windows()` record: minimized windows are listed, never filtered.

WindowsParams.description: `windows`: an optional filter; `{}` lists every window.

WindowsReply.description: `windows`: the v1 records in null mode, `WindowInfo` records in object mode.
